title: From Linear Exact Repair To Mixed-Alphabet Codes: The Bandwidth-Subpacketization Tradeoff Of Mds Array Codes
authors: Zihao Zhang, Guodong Li, Sihuang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MDS array codes achieve optimal storage efficiency in distributed storage systems, but their repair bandwidth depends critically on the sub-packetization level. While the theoretically optimal repair bandwidth (i.e., cut-set bound) of a high-rate exact-repair MDS array code is attainable with sufficiently large sub-packetization, the fundamental limits for fixed sub-packetization remain poorly understood. We study this problem for centralized linear exact repair of [MATH] failures from [MATH] helper nodes over a fixed finite field. We show that the rank profile of any linear repair scheme is constrained by two auxiliary mixed-alphabet codes. The first code is formed from the kernels of the helper projections and exists for all repair degrees; the second is formed from their row spaces and applies in the full-helper regime when [MATH]. These codes have complementary alphabet profiles, and their size and minimum-distance requirements are forced solely by the MDS property and repair correctness. This gives a unified route from classical coding-theoretic upper bounds to repair-bandwidth lower bounds. As a consequence, we obtain several explicit lower bounds via Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, and Griesmer arguments, including known bounds as corollaries. We further formulate a Delsarte-type support-enumerator LP for mixed-alphabet codes and give an exact type-compressed implementation. For fixed sub-packetization \(\ell\), this yields a polynomial-time procedure for evaluating the resulting finite-parameter lower bound.
tldr: This paper studies the tradeoff between repair bandwidth and subpacketization for classical MDS array codes in distributed storage using auxiliary mixed-alphabet codes.
motivation: MDS array codes are important for storage efficiency, but the optimal repair bandwidth for fixed subpacketization is not well understood.
method: The authors constrain the rank profile of linear exact-repair schemes via two mixed-alphabet codes derived from kernels and row spaces of helper projections, then derive lower bounds using classical coding-theoretic arguments and an LP.
result: They obtain explicit repair-bandwidth lower bounds via Singleton, Hamming, Plotkin, and Griesmer arguments, recovering known bounds as corollaries and giving a polynomial-time finite-parameter bound evaluation for fixed subpacketization.
conclusion: The work provides a unified coding-theoretic route to lower bounds on repair bandwidth for MDS array codes, but it is purely classical and not connected to quantum information.

title: Cryptanalysis And Repair Of "Decentralized Multi-authority Abe For Nc$^1$ From Bdh"
authors: Xingwang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a plaintext-recovery attack on the decentralized multi-authority attribute-based encryption construction of Datta, Komargodski, and Waters (Journal of Cryptology, 2023). The attack succeeds in the claimed static model with one corrupt authority and two users whose individual attribute sets remain unauthorized even when combined with the corrupt authority's attribute. The flaw is an incorrect extension of LSSS matrix-normalization invariance from complete secret shares to coordinate-wise ciphertext masks. A corrupt authority can expose these masks and remove identity binding from other users' decryption shares. We replace the coordinate-wise masks with independent full linear sharings of zero and prove static security under decisional bilinear Diffie-Hellman (DBDH) in the random oracle model. The repair retains the original matrix-width and row-labeling restrictions and leaves authority keys, user keys, decryption, and ciphertext size unchanged, while increasing encryption randomness and field arithmetic. We also give analogous attacks on both multi-authority attribute-based inner-product functional encryption constructions of Datta and Pal (PKC, 2023). The same modification restores correctness and matrix-substitution invariance for both variants. We prove static security of the repaired small-universe variant under asymmetric DBDH. For the large-universe variant, we identify a separate missing source-group encoding in the original reduction, formulate an augmented [MATH]-DBDH assumption, prove its hardness in the asymmetric generic bilinear group model, and give a static security reduction for the repaired scheme.
tldr: The paper breaks and repairs a decentralized multi-authority attribute-based encryption scheme by exploiting a flawed LSSS mask construction, with analogous attacks on multi-authority inner-product functional encryption.
motivation: The Datta–Komargodski–Waters multi-authority ABE for NC^1 was claimed statically secure under BDH, but the ciphertext masking step improperly extends matrix-normalization invariance from full secret shares to coordinate-wise masks, allowing a corrupt authority to strip identity binding.
method: A plaintext-recovery attack is given in the static model with one corrupt authority and two individually unauthorized users; the fix replaces coordinate-wise masks with independent full linear sharings of zero and re-proves security under DBDH in the random oracle model, plus an augmented assumption proven hard in the asymmetric generic bilinear group model.
result: The attack succeeds against the original scheme and against both Datta–Pal multi-authority inner-product FE variants; the repaired constructions retain key, decryption, and ciphertext-size properties while restoring correctness, matrix-substitution invariance, and static security.
conclusion: The work identifies a systematic normalization-invariance error in LSSS-based multi-authority designs and supplies provably secure repairs, but it lies entirely in classical public-key cryptography with no quantum information, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: Low-Dimensional Reduction Of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems With Units Described By Two Real Variables: Classification And Applications
authors: Kai Tokunaga
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables. Our classification is based on Gonz\'alez-L\'opez, Kamran, and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points and yields 28 types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems. For mean-field coupled systems with units described by two real variables, we first present a general theory on classification and low-dimensional reduction based on the mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, and then discuss applications to populations of coupled oscillators. We show that low-dimensional reduction is possible for a broad class of populations of limit-cycle oscillators, extending the previously reported reducible class of populations of Stuart-Landau oscillators to include many new models.
tldr: A classification of mean-field coupled dynamical systems with two real variables per unit, yielding 28 reducible types and applications to coupled oscillator populations.
motivation: Low-dimensional reduction is essential for understanding large networks of interacting units, and recent work on mean-field Lie-Scheffers systems motivates a systematic classification for the two-variable case.
method: The authors build on Gonzalez-Lopez, Kamran and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points to classify mean-field Lie-Scheffers coupled systems, then derive general reduction results.
result: They obtain 28 distinct types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems and show that exact low-dimensional reduction applies to a broad class of limit-cycle oscillator populations, extending beyond Stuart-Landau models.
conclusion: The classification substantially widens the class of exactly reducible mean-field oscillator networks, providing a practical toolkit for analyzing large coupled dynamical systems.

title: Methods For Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations From The Dynamics Of Quantum Systems
authors: V. I. Gerasimenko
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.
tldr: The paper reviews and develops mathematical methods for deriving nonlinear kinetic equations from the dynamics of quantum many-particle systems.
motivation: Kinetic equations provide effective descriptions of quantum many-particle systems, but their derivation from underlying evolution equations requires careful mathematical treatment.
method: The article discusses hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems and methods for deriving kinetic equations, including formulations in terms of observables and non-separable initial states.
result: It outlines key approaches to obtaining quantum kinetic equations and generalizes the quantum kinetic equation to non-separable initial states.
conclusion: The work contributes to the mathematical foundations of quantum kinetics rather than to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems as defined in the research interests.

title: Microlens-Integrated Grating Couplers For Efficient Free-Space Coupling In Silicon Photonics
authors: Simon A. Bongarz, Ryosuke Mashiko, Anne R. Kroo, Jaekwon Lee, Carson G. Valdez, David A. B. Miller, Olav Solgaard
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grating-coupler arrays are used to couple free-space light into photonic chips, but the space required for tapers and routing waveguides limits their optical fill factor. Microlens arrays can increase the effective fill factor by collecting light over a larger area and focusing it onto each grating. Separately fabricated lens arrays, however, require assembly and precise alignment to the chip. Here we integrate refractive microlenses directly with high-efficiency, normal-incidence grating couplers using two-photon polymerization. Each lens has a 100 x 100 um2 aperture and focuses incident light onto the grating. Writing the lens body at coarse resolution and the optical surface at fine resolution reduces the print time from 9 h to 19 min per lens. Under illumination by a Gaussian beam with a 276 um mode-field diameter, a printed lens increases the measured coupled power by a factor of 33 (15.2 dB) relative to the same grating before printing. Loss normalization gives an estimated lens-to-mode efficiency of 68%. The lenses show no measurable change in coupling after three 3 h thermal cycles at 150C. These results support direct printing as an approach to increasing free-space collection while simplifying lens integration in photonic systems.
tldr: The paper demonstrates direct two-photon-polymerization printing of microlenses integrated with silicon photonic grating couplers to improve free-space coupling efficiency.
motivation: Grating-coupler arrays suffer from limited optical fill factor because tapers and routing waveguides consume chip area; separately fabricated microlens arrays require precise assembly and alignment.
method: Refractive microlenses with 100 x 100 um2 apertures are printed directly onto high-efficiency normal-incidence grating couplers using two-photon polymerization, with coarse-resolution lens bodies and fine-resolution optical surfaces to reduce fabrication time.
result: Under a 276 um mode-field-diameter Gaussian beam, the printed lens increases measured coupled power by 33x (15.2 dB), with an estimated lens-to-mode efficiency of 68% and no measurable degradation after three 3 h thermal cycles at 150C.
conclusion: Direct printing of microlenses is a promising approach for increasing free-space collection efficiency and simplifying lens integration in silicon photonic systems.

title: Light Pulse Propagation Through A Dielectric Slab. I. Retarded Integral Equations And Their Local Finite-difference Solution
authors: Giancarlo Reali
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the propagation of a nonresonant light pulse normally incident on a thin dielectric slab using an integral-equation approach to electromagnetism. This emerges naturally from the microscopic picture of the material as made of polarizable atoms, confined within the material vacuum volume by their bonding interactions, each responding to the input radiation pulse as well as to the re-radiated pulses of the other atoms to which it is causally connected. The retarded integral equations are shown to be exactly equivalent to a local wave equation coupled to an auxiliary Lorentz-oscillator equation, which we solve numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme. For a slab thick enough that the front- and back-surface reflections are temporally separated, the front-surface reflectivity extracted from the simulation agrees with the Fresnel formula to within 1 percent, and the back-surface echo appears at exactly the expected round-trip delay. For a slab thinner than one optical cycle, the multiply-reflected wavelets overlap and interfere, and a full space-time map of the field directly visualizes the build-up of thin-film-like interference in the time domain. The material parameters used here are illustrative rather than fitted to measured data, and the numerical scheme is verified by an explicit grid-convergence study. In a companion paper (Paper II) the retarded integral equations are solved directly, without the local reformulation, and the two independent numerical solutions are shown to agree.
tldr: The paper derives retarded integral equations for a nonresonant light pulse propagating through a thin dielectric slab and solves them numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme.
motivation: The authors aim to give a microscopic, causally consistent description of pulse propagation and thin-film interference in dielectrics, avoiding phenomenological constitutive assumptions.
method: The material is modeled as polarizable atoms driven by the input field and by retarded fields from other atoms; the resulting integral equations are shown to be equivalent to a local wave equation coupled to a Lorentz-oscillator equation, solved via FDTD with a grid-convergence study.
result: Front-surface reflectivity matches the Fresnel formula within 1%, the back-surface echo appears at the expected round-trip delay, and for sub-cycle slabs a space-time field map visualizes time-domain build-up of thin-film interference.
conclusion: The local reformulation reproduces standard classical electromagnetism benchmarks; a companion paper solves the retarded integral equations directly and confirms agreement.

title: Encoding Trees: A Method For Producing A Variable-Length Prefix Code From Sets Of Arbitrary Size
authors: Karen Rudie Bryony H. Laporte
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we formalize a new class of binary trees called encoding trees. We extend this structure in two ways, through labelling to create the class of labelled encoding trees, and pruning to create the class of pruned encoding trees. We discuss how these two extensions can be combined to create the the class of pruned labelled encoding trees. Using the supplementary results that we prove about these classes of trees, we construct a code that uses pruned labelled encoding trees to convert a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets to a binary string. We prove that this code is a variable-length prefix code that can process any valid string of symbols from the given sequence of non-empty sets. Furthermore, we construct a code from the class of pruned labelled encoding trees that goes in the opposite direction, from binary strings to a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets of arbitrary symbols. We prove that this code is also a variable-length prefix code that can process any binary string of any length, provided that the sequence of non-empty sets is sufficiently long. We provide an equation that establishes the minimum sequence length to encode any binary string of a given length, based on that length.
tldr: The paper formalizes encoding trees and pruned labelled encoding trees to construct variable-length prefix codes between sequences of arbitrary non-empty symbol sets and binary strings.
motivation: It addresses flexible prefix coding when source symbols are drawn from a sequence of varying non-empty sets rather than a fixed alphabet.
method: The authors define classes of labelled and pruned encoding trees, prove structural properties, and use them to build encoding and decoding codes.
result: They prove both constructions yield variable-length prefix codes and derive an equation for the minimum sequence length needed to decode any binary string of a given length.
conclusion: The work is a classical coding-theory and tree-combinatorics contribution with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: $G$-crossed Braided Tensor Categories Of Twisted Modules
authors: Shun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a strongly rational vertex operator algebra and [MATH] a finite group. We prove Huang's conjecture that the categories of [MATH]-twisted [MATH]-modules, for [MATH], form a [MATH]-crossed braided fusion category. This category is faithfully [MATH]-graded, with tensor products representing the complete twisted intertwining operators of Du-Huang, the canonical pullback [MATH]-action, and crossed braiding. In particular, the associativity, coherence and rigidity required by the conjecture all hold.
tldr: The paper proves Huang's conjecture that categories of g-twisted modules over a strongly rational vertex operator algebra form a G-crossed braided fusion category.
motivation: Twisted modules and orbifold constructions in vertex operator algebra theory require a categorical framework, and Huang conjectured that these module categories assemble into a G-crossed braided fusion category; this work supplies the proof.
method: The author constructs the G-crossed braided fusion category of twisted modules, establishing the faithful G-grading, identifying tensor products with Du-Huang's complete twisted intertwining operators, defining the canonical pullback G-action, and verifying associativity, coherence and rigidity.
result: Huang's conjecture is proven: the twisted module categories form a faithfully G-graded G-crossed braided fusion category with the expected tensor structure and crossed braiding.
conclusion: The result provides a rigorous categorical foundation for orbifold and twisted-sector constructions in conformal field theory and vertex operator algebra theory.

title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization Over Decentralized Networks
authors: Haomin Bai, Junyan Sun, Quan Cheng, Yuanyu Wan, Lijun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) over decentralized networks, where workers collaborate to learn robust models by minimizing the maximum local risk. Existing methods optimize only dual-regularized surrogates and establish guarantees for a globally averaged model that is not available to workers. In this paper, we directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized (SemiDec) and fully decentralized (Dec) settings. A key difficulty is that applying the primal-dual decomposition from centralized GDRO yields worker-dependent losses whose evaluation requires unavailable cross-worker information. To address this challenge, we develop a novel error decomposition that recasts decentralized GDRO as (i) a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem and a prediction-with-expert-advice problem in SemiDec, and as (ii) two coupled D-OCO problems in Dec, with discrepancy terms capturing inconsistencies among local decisions. By isolating consensus errors in analysis, we develop modular frameworks that support different consensus routines. We then establish the per-worker convergence guarantees for optimizing the original GDRO objective over decentralized networks. Instantiations with accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip achieve an [MATH] convergence rate over [MATH] update rounds, while experiments demonstrate improved worst-worker performance over baselines.
tldr: This paper develops decentralized optimization algorithms for group distributionally robust optimization with per-worker convergence guarantees.
motivation: Existing GDRO methods over decentralized networks optimize dual-regularized surrogates and guarantee performance only for an unavailable globally averaged model.
method: The authors directly optimize the original GDRO objective by decomposing decentralized GDRO into decentralized online convex optimization and expert-advice subproblems, with discrepancy terms capturing local decision inconsistencies.
result: They establish per-worker convergence guarantees and show that accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip instantiations achieve improved worst-worker performance over baselines in experiments.
conclusion: The work provides modular convergence frameworks for decentralized GDRO, but it is a classical distributed optimization paper with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sat Sampling At Scale Via GPU-based Boolean Constraint Propagation
authors: Alexander Nadel, Yogev Shalmon, Ofer Strichman
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constrained-random verification tests hardware designs by sampling solutions of Boolean formulas. Existing samplers largely follow one of two approaches: CPU-based SAT samplers (e.g., CMSGen), which remain effective even at rare targets but offer limited throughput, and GPU-based gradient samplers, which achieve high throughput at high-probability targets but collapse at rare ones. We introduce Gpap-S, the first GPU sampler built on Boolean constraint propagation (BCP). At its core is Gpap, a new GPU engine for BCP that efficiently propagates many independent partial assignments concurrently on a shared Boolean formula. This capability allows Gpap-S to combine the rare-target robustness of SAT-based sampling with the throughput of GPU parallelism by exploring thousands of decide-and-propagate trajectories simultaneously. On the benchmark families used to evaluate prior GPU gradient samplers, Gpap-S is 2.2-18.7x faster at the high-probability targets considered in those evaluations. At rare targets, where those samplers often fail to generate any samples, Gpap-S achieves a geometric-mean speedup of roughly two orders of magnitude. Across all benchmarks, Gpap-S is also 83.4-1,571x faster than the CPU-based CMSGen. This throughput does not come at the expense of sample quality: under Barbarik, the statistical tester used to evaluate CMSGen, Gpap-S is accepted on every instance we test, as is CMSGen. We release Gpap as a reusable GPU library for high-throughput BCP.
tldr: Gpap-S is the first GPU-accelerated SAT sampler built on Boolean constraint propagation, achieving large throughput gains over CPU-based and GPU gradient samplers while retaining robustness at rare targets.
motivation: Constrained-random verification requires sampling solutions of Boolean formulas; existing CPU SAT samplers are robust but slow, while GPU gradient samplers are fast at high-probability targets but fail at rare ones, motivating a GPU-native BCP sampler.
method: The authors introduce Gpap, a reusable GPU engine that propagates thousands of independent partial assignments concurrently over a shared Boolean formula, and build Gpap-S on top of it to explore many decide-and-propagate trajectories in parallel.
result: Gpap-S is 2.2-18.7x faster than prior GPU gradient samplers at high-probability targets, roughly two orders of magnitude faster at rare targets, and 83.4-1,571x faster than CMSGen, while passing the Barbarik statistical tester on every instance.
conclusion: GPU-based Boolean constraint propagation makes SAT-based sampling both robust and high-throughput, and Gpap is released as a reusable library for high-throughput BCP.

title: Regular Syndrome Decoding Is Easier Than Previously Estimated
authors: Jiseung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Changmin Lee, Hochang Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Regular Syndrome Decoding (RSD) problem is a structured variant of classical Syndrome Decoding and underlies a growing number of efficient cryptographic constructions, including zero knowledge protocols, pseudorandom correlation generators, and MPC in the Head signatures. Although RSD is generally believed to be computationally hard, recent works have shown that algebraic attacks can outperform information set decoding on important RSD parameter regimes. Building on this line of work, we revisit the concrete hardness of RSD and show that many widely used parameter sets are substantially easier to solve than previously estimated. This improvement stems from a refined hybrid algebraic attack that exposes and removes a previously overlooked source of concrete complexity: the joint blockwise placement of zero coordinate guesses and syndrome based variable eliminations. Rather than treating the two guessing stages and linear elimination as largely separate choices, our method coordinates them across all regular blocks so that the guessing penalty is balanced while sufficient equations are retained for linearization. This gives a systematic block balancing principle for the entire guess reduce solve pipeline. We reassess several RSD based applications, including Ferret, Wolverine, and committed VOLE. Our estimates place at least one parameter set per application below its 128 bit target, with losses approaching 67 bits. On PCG benchmarks, we improve previous best attack costs by up to 29.77 and 25.91 bits over non binary and binary fields, respectively. Moreover, for the revised 128 bit PCG parameter sets of Liu et al. evaluated here, estimated attack costs are all below [MATH] field operations. These results substantially revise the concrete security landscape of RSD and indicate that several existing parameter choices overestimate the hardness of their underlying RSD instances.
tldr: The paper improves algebraic attacks on the Regular Syndrome Decoding problem, showing that many cryptographic parameter sets are easier to break than previously estimated.
motivation: RSD underlies efficient cryptographic constructions such as zero-knowledge protocols, pseudorandom correlation generators, and MPC-in-the-head signatures, so accurately assessing its concrete hardness is important for parameter selection.
method: The authors introduce a refined hybrid algebraic attack that jointly coordinates blockwise zero-coordinate guessing with syndrome-based variable elimination, balancing the guessing penalty while retaining enough equations for linearization.
result: They find that at least one parameter set per application falls below its 128-bit target, with losses approaching 67 bits, and improve prior attack costs by up to 29.77 bits over non-binary fields and 25.91 bits over binary fields.
conclusion: The concrete security landscape of RSD is substantially revised, indicating that several existing parameter choices overestimate the hardness of their underlying RSD instances.

title: When Are We Near Nash? Certifying Solutions In General-Sum Games
authors: Longbo Huang Boning Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heuristic solvers for general-sum extensive-form games produce a stream of iterates, and practice reports the NashGap of the returned profile. We ask what a solver can know about its own iterates from the regret accumulators and the terminal-distribution accumulators its updates already maintain. In two-player games the NashGap of a weighted average strategy equals, at the maximizing player, the weighted external regret plus a signed value correction. Bounding the regret by the running counterfactual-regret accumulator gives an online certificate whose cost per checkpoint is linear in the number of terminal histories. The certificate stays sound under alternating updates and in games with three or more players. The mismatch between what alternation evaluates and what the averages record enters as one signed comparator term, maximized in a single backward pass per player whose comparator weight is nonzero. The bound is read off the regret state, with no best response against the average. Run a portfolio of training-free regret-matching solvers, output the iterate with the smallest certificate, and verify that iterate once. On the benchmark's biased Leduc family a pool of sixteen training-free solvers, seven original and nine recent variants, solves [MATH] of the [MATH] instances at threshold [MATH] this way, matching the trajectory-minimum union of the solvers. The same protocol solves [MATH] of the [MATH] pre-registered held-out instances and [MATH] again on a third set of [MATH] instances that no earlier stage used. The zero-best-response certificate certifies all [MATH] in-sample solves and all [MATH] fresh ones, and [MATH] of the [MATH] held-out ones. Its exact-comparator refinement certifies every solve in the three sets. The certificate states both and attributes its bound. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: The paper derives an online certificate for the Nash gap of iterates produced by regret-matching solvers in general-sum extensive-form games, using regret accumulators and a signed value correction.
motivation: Heuristic solvers produce iterates without guarantees, and practitioners need a way to assess solution quality without expensive best-response computation.
method: The Nash gap of a weighted average strategy is expressed as weighted external regret plus a signed comparator term, yielding a certificate computable from existing accumulators with per-checkpoint cost linear in terminal histories.
result: A portfolio of sixteen training-free solvers solves nearly all benchmark Leduc instances when selecting the iterate with the smallest certificate, and the certificate certifies the solves in-sample and on held-out sets.
conclusion: The certificate provides a practical, sound online verification tool for Nash equilibrium approximation in general-sum games, with exact-comparator refinement certifying all solves.

title: Order-Specified Quaternion Cp Decomposition: Models, Algorithms, And Applications
authors: Jifei Miao, Niansheng Tang, Michael K. Ng, Juan Han, Kit Ian Kou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor CP decomposition serves as a fundamental tool for representing multiway data. While quaternion tensors are well suited to modeling color visual data, extending CP decomposition to the quaternion domain is nontrivial due to the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication. This paper develops an order-specified quaternion CP decomposition (OS-QCP) for third-order tensors, allowing all three factor matrices to be quaternion-valued and explicitly incorporating their multiplication order into the model. We show that different multiplication orders can yield different OS-QCP ranks for the same quaternion tensor, characterize the permutation and quaternion scaling indeterminacies, and establish a sufficient condition for essential uniqueness for any prescribed multiplication order. An explicit example further shows that OS-QCP rank can depend on the multiplication order even when the complex representation of the quaternion tensor admits an essentially unique CP decomposition. An alternating least-squares (ALS) algorithm is derived by expressing quaternion left and right multiplication as real linear operators, reducing each factor update to real least-squares problems. To accommodate order dependence in tensor completion, we further introduce an order-ensemble quaternion CP (OE-QCP) model that incorporates different multiplication orders through nonnegative weights. The model jointly estimates three quaternion factor matrices and the order weights, with each single-order OS-QCP model included as a special case. The resulting completion problem is solved by a parallel row-wise masked ALS algorithm. Experiments on color video inpainting demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of the proposed method.
tldr: The paper introduces an order-specified quaternion CP decomposition (OS-QCP) for third-order quaternion tensors, together with an order-ensemble variant (OE-QCP) for tensor completion and an ALS solver, applied to color video inpainting.
motivation: Quaternion tensors naturally model color visual data, but extending CP decomposition to the quaternion domain is difficult because quaternion multiplication is noncommutative, so the order of factor multiplication must be handled explicitly.
method: All three factor matrices are allowed to be quaternion-valued with an explicit multiplication order; the authors characterize permutation and quaternion scaling indeterminacies, give a sufficient uniqueness condition, and derive ALS updates by representing quaternion left/right multiplication as real linear operators. An order-ensemble model with nonnegative weights is solved by a parallel row-wise masked ALS algorithm.
result: Different multiplication orders can give different OS-QCP ranks for the same quaternion tensor, even when the complex representation admits an essentially unique CP decomposition; experiments on color video inpainting show competitive performance.
conclusion: Order-specified quaternion CP decomposition provides a principled and effective framework for multiway quaternion data analysis, with rank dependence on multiplication order as a key structural feature.

title: Prompt Injection Through Forensic Evidence: A Taxonomy And Proof Of Concept Of Anti-Forensic Attacks On LLM-Assisted Digital Investigations
authors: Frank Breitinger, Jan Gruber, Christopher Hargreaves, Jan-Niclas Hilgert, Ga\"etan Michelet, Mark Scanlon
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering digital forensics as examination assistants and autonomous agents. Digital forensics inverts the usual setting for indirect prompt injection: the evidence under analysis is attacker-controlled by definition, and the examiner is obliged to read it closely. This makes the reasoning layer a new anti-forensic target, next to the classical ones of data and tools. Classical anti-forensic taxonomies do not cover it, and prompt injection defences do not anticipate it. We extend the anti-forensic model to reflect the manipulation of reasoning, and present a taxonomy of attacks carried through adversarial evidence: an attacker selects an objective, a technique, a payload location, and a concealment method. We observe a perception gap, i.e., the fact that deterministic tools, the human examiner, and the model perceive the same evidence differently, which is what lets an injection reach the model unseen by the examiner. We demonstrate three attacks against an LLM-assisted analysis pipeline, changing a reported conclusion, writing attacker-chosen content to the analyst's workstation, and causing outbound network traffic, each driven only by text planted on the seized device. Mitigations to these attacks are also proposed.
tldr: The paper extends anti-forensic taxonomies to cover prompt-injection attacks that manipulate the reasoning layer of LLM-assisted digital forensic investigations, demonstrated through three proof-of-concept attacks.
motivation: LLMs are entering digital forensics as examination assistants, but evidence in forensics is attacker-controlled by definition, creating a new attack surface on the reasoning layer that classical anti-forensic models and existing prompt-injection defences do not address.
method: The authors extend the anti-forensic model with a taxonomy of adversarial-evidence attacks (objective, technique, payload location, concealment) and demonstrate three concrete attacks against an LLM-assisted analysis pipeline driven only by text planted on a seized device.
result: The attacks succeed in altering a reported conclusion, writing attacker-chosen content to the analyst's workstation, and triggering outbound network traffic, illustrating a 'perception gap' between deterministic tools, the human examiner, and the model.
conclusion: Reasoning-layer manipulation should be treated as a genuine anti-forensic target, and the paper proposes mitigations to defend LLM-assisted digital investigations against adversarial evidence.

title: Boot-AVT: Asymptotically Anytime-Valid Testing With Degenerate U-Statistics Via Bootstrap
authors: Jixuan Liu, Long Feng, Liuhua Peng, Zhaojun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonparametric tests are based on [MATH]-statistics that are degenerate under the null hypothesis. We develop Boot-AVT, a bootstrap procedure for asymptotically anytime-valid testing with these statistics. Using Brownian scaling and time inversion for the limiting Gaussian chaos process, we show that logarithmically penalized maxima over observed and future sample sizes have a common limiting null distribution. A quadratic multiplier bootstrap estimates the corresponding critical values. We also develop Boot-AVT-Multi for joint testing with multiple kernels. For both procedures, we establish uniform consistency of the bootstrap critical values, explicit bounds on size distortion, and asymptotic size [MATH] over an unbounded monitoring horizon as the monitoring start tends to infinity. Under fixed alternatives, we derive finite-horizon power bounds and establish power one with finite expected stopping times. Simulation studies evaluate finite-sample size and power in goodness-of-fit, two-sample and independence testing, and real-data analyses compare stopping times.
tldr: Boot-AVT is a bootstrap procedure for asymptotically anytime-valid testing with degenerate U-statistics, using Brownian scaling of the limiting Gaussian chaos process and a quadratic multiplier bootstrap for critical values.
motivation: Many nonparametric tests rely on U-statistics that are degenerate under the null, and there is a need for tests whose validity holds uniformly over unbounded monitoring horizons (anytime-valid inference).
method: The authors show that logarithmically penalized maxima of the Gaussian chaos process over observed and future sample sizes share a common limiting null distribution, and estimate critical values via a quadratic multiplier bootstrap; an extension, Boot-AVT-Multi, handles joint testing with multiple kernels.
result: They establish uniform consistency of bootstrap critical values, explicit bounds on size distortion, asymptotic size control over unbounded horizons, and finite-horizon power bounds with power one and finite expected stopping times under fixed alternatives; simulations cover goodness-of-fit, two-sample and independence testing.
conclusion: Boot-AVT provides a principled, asymptotically anytime-valid framework for degenerate U-statistic testing with multiple kernels, supported by theory and empirical stopping-time comparisons.

title: Diffusion Sensitivity Geometry And Strong Duality For Optimal Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
authors: Daniel Alabi Tue Do
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing approaches to differential privacy in diffusion models rely on loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, leading to unnecessary estimation error. We develop a framework for the optimal privacy-utility tradeoff of ideal diffusion denoisers, replacing conservative bounds with exact sensitivity characterizations and provably optimal noise calibration. First, we show that worst-case sensitivity over datasets of arbitrary size can be characterized exactly using only two records. For a data domain of size [MATH], this reduces the analysis to at most [MATH] constraints, regardless of dataset size. Our characterization can be arbitrarily tighter than conventional diameter-based sensitivity bounds, revealing potentially unbounded improvements in noise calibration. Second, we obtain exact privacy guarantees for R\'enyi, approximate, and Gaussian differential privacy, as well as mutual-information privacy for binary records, avoiding the looseness of previous generic privacy conversions. Finally, we show that the minimum achievable weighted mean-squared error can be computed through a semidefinite program and prove strong duality, providing certificates of global optimality.
tldr: The paper develops exact sensitivity characterizations and optimal noise calibration for differentially private diffusion models, with strong-duality certificates for privacy-utility tradeoffs.
motivation: Existing differential privacy approaches for diffusion models use loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, causing unnecessary estimation error.
method: The authors characterize worst-case sensitivity using only two records, derive exact guarantees for Rényi, approximate, Gaussian, and mutual-information privacy, and formulate the minimum weighted mean-squared error as a semidefinite program.
result: They show sensitivity can be arbitrarily tighter than diameter-based bounds, obtain exact privacy guarantees avoiding generic conversion looseness, and prove strong duality for globally optimal certificates.
conclusion: The work provides a principled optimization framework for privacy-utility tradeoffs in diffusion models, but it is a classical differential-privacy/ML paper with no direct quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems content.

title: Model-based Computational Study Of Reactive Fluid Systems Using Transfer Operator Methods
authors: Anja G\"obel, Anna Kl\"unker, Alexandra von Kameke, Kathrin Padberg-Gehle
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many industrial applications one aims for the design of efficient chemical reactions. This is often done using experimental analysis of the reactors in combination with numerical twins. However, the simultaneous modeling of flow, mixing and chemical reaction remains a complicated task because the computational costs are still significant and oftentimes prohibitive. Here, we model and analyze mixing processes of chemical substances by a transfer operator method using the Lagrangian trajectories of passive particles. In practice, we represent the spatial distributions of the chemical species concentrations by density vectors. These are evolved by means of a stochastic transition matrix, which is obtained as a numerical approximation of a transfer operator. In a further step, we model the reaction of the fluids by specific update rules of the density vectors. The method is applicable for closed and open example systems and different chemical processes such as competitive consecutive reactions. We demonstrate that the dynamic processes are reflected well by this method. Furthermore, we evaluate the interdependence of the reaction fronts with Lagrangian coherent structures which we define using set-oriented methods that also work well on three dimensional data.
tldr: The paper models mixing and chemical reactions in fluid systems using transfer operator methods built from Lagrangian particle trajectories.
motivation: Simultaneously modeling flow, mixing, and chemical reaction in industrial reactor design is computationally expensive, motivating cheaper data-driven surrogates.
method: Species concentrations are represented as density vectors evolved by a stochastic transition matrix approximating a transfer operator, with reaction modeled via update rules on these vectors; reaction fronts are compared to Lagrangian coherent structures found by set-oriented methods.
result: The approach reproduces the dynamics of closed and open example systems, including competitive consecutive reactions, and reveals interdependence between reaction fronts and coherent structures, including in 3D data.
conclusion: Transfer-operator-based density evolution is a viable, computationally efficient tool for analyzing reactive fluid mixing, though it is purely classical fluid mechanics.

title: A Structure-Preserving Scheme For Computing The Gradient Of The Eikonal Equation
authors: Shingyu Leung Ka Lun Leung
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a first-order, structure-preserving method for directly computing the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation in smooth first-arrival regions. The method combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) in a Godunov-type upwind discretization with spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration. This construction gives a tangent residual and keeps every iterate on [MATH] without projection or normalization. The SLERP discretization exactly preserves a family of curved orientation equilibria. Removing the background discretization bias improves absolute orientation accuracy near these equilibria, allowing a prescribed error tolerance to be reached on a coarser grid. We prove the equilibrium-preservation property and, separately, a smaller angular error for SFE than normalized Euler in a one-cell relaxation under the stated step-size condition. Two- and three-dimensional experiments examine convergence, geometric preservation, and computational cost. Comparisons with gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes show more accurate directions on the same grid in the curved media considered. The method provides direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential use in adjoint-based inverse problems.
tldr: A first-order structure-preserving numerical scheme computes the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation directly, keeping iterates on the unit sphere via SLERP-based upwind discretization and spherical forward Euler integration.
motivation: Gradient recovery from scalar traveltime solutions is inaccurate; the authors seek a scheme that directly produces accurate direction fields while exactly preserving curved orientation equilibria without projection or renormalization.
method: The scheme combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) within a Godunov-type upwind discretization with a spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration, yielding a tangent residual that keeps every iterate on the unit sphere; equilibrium preservation and a reduced angular error bound are proved.
result: Two- and three-dimensional experiments show improved absolute orientation accuracy near curved equilibria, coarser grids meeting prescribed tolerances, and more accurate directions than gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes at comparable cost.
conclusion: The method supplies accurate direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential application to adjoint-based inverse problems.

title: Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning The Flow Of Autonomous Systems By Conjugation To Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows
authors: Andrew Qing He
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE [MATH] as a conjugate [MATH] of an explicitly integrable reference flow [MATH] by an invertible neural network [MATH], the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A [MATH] conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of [MATH]. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving [MATH] cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to [MATH] and sampled log-uniformly in [MATH] around an equilibrium, with the anchors [MATH], [MATH]; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation [MATH] and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of [MATH].
tldr: The paper introduces a neural-network representation of autonomous ODE flows as conjugates of explicitly integrable reference flows, with a training recipe for learning dynamical invariants.
motivation: The authors aim to learn accurate flow maps for autonomous dynamical systems while preserving structural properties such as eigenvalues, periodic orbits, and symplectic structure by construction.
method: They represent the flow as an invertible neural-network conjugacy to a parametrized integrable reference flow and train it using a relative push-forward residual with invariant initialization and symplectic constraints.
result: The method recovers eigenvalue spectra, action-angle variables, and symplectic flows for several low-dimensional systems, though data-only identification of Van der Pol dynamics remains limited by network expressivity.
conclusion: Neural vector field transformations provide a structured way to learn autonomous flows with inherited phase-portrait invariants, but the work is classical dynamical-systems machine learning rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: New Matrix-weighted Norm Inequalities And Extrapolation
authors: Pengfei Yin Guixiang Hong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a new type of matrix-weighted theory and show the corresponding Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorems by means of noncommutative maximal inequalities. We introduce a new matrix [MATH] condition following Volberg's geometric formulation, and characterize it via a noncommutative Hardy--Littlewood maximal inequality. We then establish a noncommutative analogue of Rubio de Francia's abstract extrapolation theorem for trace-finite von Neumann algebras. The argument extends to [MATH] through pointwise matrix operations. This yields the desired extrapolation results for individual operators and maximal families, with applications to matrix-weighted boundedness of Calder\'on--Zygmund operators.
tldr: The paper develops a new matrix-weighted norm theory and proves noncommutative Rubio de Francia extrapolation theorems for trace-finite von Neumann algebras.
motivation: Matrix-weighted inequalities and extrapolation are central tools in harmonic analysis, and the authors aim to extend them to the noncommutative setting where classical pointwise arguments fail.
method: They introduce a new matrix A_p condition in Volberg's geometric formulation, characterize it through a noncommutative Hardy–Littlewood maximal inequality, and prove an abstract extrapolation theorem for trace-finite von Neumann algebras, extending to A_infty via pointwise matrix operations.
result: Extrapolation results are obtained for individual operators and maximal families, yielding matrix-weighted boundedness of Calderón–Zygmund operators.
conclusion: The work provides a noncommutative analog of Rubio de Francia extrapolation and new matrix-weighted bounds for singular integral operators.

title: On The Gradient Conjecture At Infinity: Finite Spherical Length For Gradient Trajectories Of Definable Potentials
authors: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every open [MATH] the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory [MATH], [MATH], of a definable [MATH]-potential [MATH] has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable [MATH]-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
tldr: The paper proves that gradient trajectories of definable potentials in o-minimal structures have finite spherical projection length, yielding directional convergence and applications to deep neural network training flows.
motivation: The work addresses the gradient conjecture at infinity and the definable Thom gradient conjecture for gradient flows of definable potentials, with motivation from understanding convergence of training dynamics in deep neural networks.
method: Using o-minimality and definable geometry, the authors analyze arbitrary solutions of the gradient flow differential equation and bound the total angular motion of their spherical projections.
result: For every definable C^1 potential, every gradient trajectory has a finite-length spherical projection and hence converges directionally, even when the trajectory is unbounded or nonunique.
conclusion: The theorem affirmatively resolves the gradient conjecture at infinity and the definable Thom gradient conjecture, and implies directional convergence of DNN training flows for definable activation and loss functions.

title: Third And Fourth Moment Phenomena For Monochromatic Edges And Applications To Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
authors: Siva Athreya, Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya, Yogesh Dahiya, Karambir Das, Spandan Ghoshal, Sourish Maniyar, Elizabeth Sara Roy

We characterize the asymptotic normality of [MATH], after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed [MATH], asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero. These results identify three distinct regimes for moment characterizations of Gaussian convergence, determined by the coloring probability. tldr: The paper characterizes asymptotic normality of the number of monochromatic edges in randomly colored graphs via third and fourth moment conditions, with applications to graph-based two-sample tests.
motivation: Moment conditions (especially the fourth moment theorem) are standard tools for proving Gaussian convergence of graph-based functionals; the authors aim to determine when weaker third moment conditions suffice and how coloring probabilities alter these characterizations.
method: The authors analyze subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments of the monochromatic edge count for independent red/blue vertex colorings, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality across different regimes of the coloring probability, including a sparse regime.

title: Bistable Dynamics And Complete Classifications Of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes Aegypti And Aedes Albopictus
authors: Lei Niu, Yi Wang, Xizhuang Xie, Bo Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. Consequently, bistable dynamics naturally emerge, which provides a rigorous theoretical validation of the numerical simulation results reported in the aforementioned work. Building on this, we further derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics. In addition, we carry out a comprehensive analysis of how seasonal switching mechanisms govern the competitive outcomes between these two mosquito species, thereby offering insights into their ecological coexistence and potential displacement.
tldr: The paper rigorously establishes bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics for a seasonally forced competition model between two mosquito species.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a rigorous theoretical validation of earlier numerical simulations of competition between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus under favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts.
method: Using Floquet theory, they prove instability of the unique positive periodic solution and derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics, including analysis of seasonal switching effects.
result: The unique positive periodic solution is shown to be unstable, which naturally yields bistable dynamics, and the complete global dynamics are classified with ecological interpretations of coexistence and displacement.
conclusion: Seasonal switching mechanisms govern competitive outcomes between the two mosquito species, offering ecological insight into their coexistence and potential displacement.

title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform Of Complex Radon Measures On $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
authors: Vaishakh Jayaprakash Tathagata Banerjee
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on [MATH] to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on [MATH] under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in [MATH] using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.
tldr: The paper characterizes continuous wavelet transforms of complex Radon measures on R^d and establishes an isometric Banach-algebra isomorphism with a new norm.
motivation: The work aims to extend wavelet transform theory from functions to complex Radon measures under suitable wavelet regularity assumptions.
method: It derives necessary and sufficient conditions for a measurable function to be a continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure, defines a new norm on such transforms, and proves an isometric isomorphism to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution.
result: The authors obtain a restricted wavelet inversion formula for measures and, under additional hypotheses, a reconstruction formula for measures of closed rectangles in R^d, supported by examples.
conclusion: The paper provides a functional-analytic framework for wavelet transforms of measures, but it is purely mathematical and has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Precision Coexistence: Angular-Spectral Region Constrained Waveform Design For Mimo-isac
authors: Syed Ali Haider Shirazi, Taejoon Kim, David J. Love, Sergiy A. Vorobyov
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a dual-function waveform design framework for multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments. In such environments, the dual-function waveform must coexist with legacy systems, such as localized positioning sensors, maritime radar networks, and satellite communication links, that occupy specific frequency bands and angular sectors. To enable precision coexistence, we incorporate localized angular-spectral region constraints that suppress beamformed energy only within the angle-frequency regions occupied by each legacy system, while preserving the spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) available outside those regions. The resulting waveform design problem is formulated as a nonconvex optimization problem and solved using a low-complexity majorization--minimization alternating direction method of multipliers (MM--ADMM) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides precise legacy-system protection while maintaining robust radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.
tldr: The paper proposes a constrained waveform design framework for MIMO integrated sensing and communication systems to coexist with legacy wireless systems.
motivation: MIMO-ISAC systems operating in congested electromagnetic environments must avoid interfering with legacy radar, positioning, and satellite communication systems.
method: It formulates a nonconvex optimization problem with localized angular-spectral region constraints and solves it using an MM-ADMM algorithm.
result: Simulations show precise protection of legacy systems while maintaining radar sensing and multi-user communication performance.
conclusion: The framework enables precision coexistence for MIMO-ISAC through angular-spectral region constrained waveform design.

title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication Through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
authors: Neophytos Charalambides, Mert Pilanci, Alfred O. Hero III
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. Specifically, we propose using a non-uniform sampling distribution constructed from the leverage scores of the two matrices, and characterize the associated approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm; which is well-known to better characterize the downstream error when the matrix product operator is applied to an input vector. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.
tldr: The paper proposes a randomized approximate matrix multiplication algorithm using leverage-score-based joint sampling and analyzes spectral-norm error bounds.
motivation: Approximate matrix multiplication via random sampling is important for large-scale numerical linear algebra, and leverage scores can provide non-uniform sampling with better error control.
method: The authors construct a joint non-uniform sampling distribution from leverage scores of the two input matrices and derive probability error bounds for the resulting approximation in spectral norm.
result: They characterize the approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm and provide probabilistic guarantees, while relating the approach to data-oblivious sampling and graph sparsification.
conclusion: The work advances classical randomized matrix algorithms but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Combining Long-Term Memory And LLMs Comes At A High Cost: From Prompt Injection To Persistent Compromise
authors: Pedro H. Barcha Correia, Matheus Azevedo de S\'a, Paulo H. Gomes de Senna, Giovanni Mandel Martignago, Victor Takashi Hayashi, Charles Christian Miers, Marcos A. Simplicio Jr
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The widespread adoption of generative artificial intelligence in recent years has brought a parallel rise in prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. By embedding malicious instructions, these exploits manipulate language models to bypass intended behavior and operational boundaries. In traditional chatbots, such attacks are confined to a single session because state memory is not preserved across conversations. However, persistent memory features in modern conversational interfaces enable cross-session attack propagation, establishing a threat vector known as memory injection. This work explores this emerging vulnerability in leading LLM-as-a-service platforms, highlighting its real-world severity and the need for countermeasures. While existing literature focuses on violations tailored to specific platform features, we present a general threat model. We demonstrate that all NIST attack goals are collectively achievable across ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash under this model. We also show that memory injections can exploit multiple attack vectors, including personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected resources. Our findings reveal that all evaluated services can be manipulated to persistently spread disinformation, generate harmful content, or simulate offline unresponsiveness, even in fresh sessions. In the particular case of Claude, shared-memory features allow an attacker to compromise multiple users within an organization and also exfiltrate user prompts. To address these vulnerabilities, we derive defense mechanisms from our proposed threat model and foundational cybersecurity principles. Our analysis indicates that nearly half of these mitigations remain unimplemented across the target services. Datasets and attack artifacts are available at [URL].
tldr: The paper analyzes cross-session memory injection vulnerabilities in commercial LLM-as-a-service platforms and proposes mitigations.
motivation: Persistent memory features in conversational AI enable prompt-injection attacks to propagate across sessions, creating a new threat vector not covered by prior session-bound analyses.
method: The authors introduce a general threat model for memory injection and evaluate it against ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 3 Flash across multiple memory vectors, including personal memories, projects, skills, organization instructions, and MCP-connected resources.
result: They show that all NIST attack goals are collectively achievable, enabling persistent disinformation, harmful content generation, simulated unresponsiveness, multi-user compromise via shared memory, and prompt exfiltration in Claude.
conclusion: The work derives defense mechanisms from the threat model and finds that nearly half remain unimplemented across the evaluated services.

title: Strict Equality In Higher Identity Types: Axioms, Completeness, Decidability
authors: Keri D'angelo, Liron Cohen, Luke Serafin, Dexter Kozen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.28906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning about higher identity types uses two equalities, strict equality and equivalence of cells witnessed by a path. Strict equality is a congruence for every operation on cells, but associativity and the identity laws fail for it. Equivalence of cells satisfies those two laws, but it is not a congruence. Representations of higher identity types often conflate equational properties that hold strictly with those that hold only up to a path. We separate the two and axiomatize the former, introducing SEq, an equational theory generated by eleven axioms for strict equality between cells. We prove soundness and completeness for homotopy models, and completeness already over finite CW-complexes. Nine of these axioms form a strongly normalizing rewrite system whose normal forms are unique up to picture equivalence, and the resulting word problem is decidable in exponential time. We also give presheaf models over a cubical base category in which composition arises from a pushout in the base category itself, without requiring Kan filling structure. The same pushout structure provides explicit higher-dimensional witnesses for associativity and the identity laws.
tldr: The paper introduces an equational theory SEq for strict equality in higher identity types and proves soundness, completeness, decidability, and presheaf-model results.
motivation: Reasoning about higher identity types conflates strict equality, which is a congruence but lacks associativity/identity laws, with path equivalence, which satisfies those laws but is not a congruence.
method: The authors axiomatize strict equality between cells using eleven axioms, prove soundness and completeness for homotopy models and finite CW-complexes, and give a strongly normalizing rewrite system for nine axioms.
result: The rewrite system has unique normal forms up to picture equivalence and yields an exponential-time decision procedure for the word problem; presheaf models over a cubical base category provide higher-dimensional witnesses for associativity and identity laws.
conclusion: This work separates strict equality from path equivalence in higher identity types, providing a rigorous axiomatic, computational, and semantic foundation for strict equational reasoning.

title: Correlated Quantal Response Equilibrium: A New Equilibrium Notion For Human-AI Strategic Interactions
authors: Zehao Zhao, Rahul Jain, Vijay Subramanian
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modeling of the behavior of agents in strategic environments and the prediction of the resulting outcomes has long been a challenging problem; this has been the focus of game theory. The introduction of AI agents as human-aids or as sole decision-makers expands the underlying question: Can we model behavior and predict outcomes of strategic games that involve a mix of AI agents and human players? As an initial answer, we propose Correlated Quantal Response Equilibrium (CQRE) that combines and generalizes classical solution concepts such as Quantal Response Equilibrium and Correlated Equilibrium. We answer questions of existence and propose a method for computing the CQRE that is a best fit to a given joint action distribution. We demonstrate the empirical effectiveness of CQRE predictions using a diverse collection of complex general-sum games, including high-rank and large-action two-player games, challenging multiplayer games, and a large-scale extension of the Selten--Chmura setting to AI--AI and human--AI play.
tldr: The paper introduces Correlated Quantal Response Equilibrium (CQRE), a new solution concept for modeling strategic interactions between humans and AI agents, generalizing quantal response equilibrium and correlated equilibrium.
motivation: Game-theoretic modeling of mixed human-AI strategic environments is poorly captured by classical equilibrium notions, which assume fully rational agents and cannot predict boundedly rational human behavior alongside AI decision-makers.
method: The authors define CQRE by combining quantal response (bounded rationality) with correlated equilibrium (a mediator/signal structure), prove existence, and develop a computation method that fits CQRE to a given joint action distribution.
result: CQRE predictions are empirically validated on diverse general-sum games, including high-rank and large-action two-player games, challenging multiplayer games, and a large-scale Selten-Chmura extension for AI-AI and human-AI play.
conclusion: CQRE offers a principled and computationally practical equilibrium notion for predicting outcomes in human-AI strategic settings, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Broadcasting In Centimeter-Wave Gigantic Mimo Systems: Beam Shaping Is All You Need
authors: Boyu Ning, Yike Xie, Jaebum Park, Songjie Yang, Weidong Mei, Emil Bj\"ornson, Robert W. Heath Jr
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beamforming is a key enabling technology for centimeter-wave Gigantic MIMO (G-MIMO) systems, using antenna arrays to generate wide beams for cell-wide broadcasting or narrow beams for data transmission. This paper presents a novel for designing environment-aware broadcast beams (i.e., beams for common control information delivery, as in 5G SSB). As a case study, we shape a in the vertical plane to approximate uniform electromagnetic power distribution across the ground, thereby enhancing broadcast coverage quality. We first propose a geometric broadcasting model that, through coordinate transformation, relates base station height, beam spread, maximum service distance, and downtilt angle. Building on this model and the signal propagation model, we formulate the beam shaping problem as a non-convex optimization problem that aims to maximize ground-level coverage. To solve it, we develop a generalized optimization framework. We reformulate the problem into a matrix representation, equivalently transforming it into a target pursuit optimization (TPO) problem. Using variable substitution, the objective is convexified into a quadratically constrained quadratic program, and the non-convex rank constraint is handled via successive convex approximation, decomposing the problem into iteratively solved subproblems. We provide complexity and convergence analyses for the proposed algorithm. Numerical simulations confirm that the optimization effectively shapes the intended beam pattern and that the proposed prostrate beam yields significant performance gains, including substantially extended coverage distance, over conventional wide-beam benchmarks.
tldr: The paper designs environment-aware broadcast beams for centimeter-wave Gigantic MIMO systems by formulating ground-coverage maximization as a non-convex beam-shaping problem and solving it via successive convex approximation.
motivation: G-MIMO base stations must deliver common control information (e.g., 5G SSB) over wide areas, so broadcast beams should approximate uniform power distribution on the ground rather than using conventional wide-beam patterns.
method: A geometric broadcasting model relates base-station height, beam spread, maximum service distance, and downtilt angle; the beam-shaping problem is recast as a target-pursuit optimization, convexified via variable substitution into a QCQP, with the rank constraint handled by successive convex approximation.
result: Numerical simulations confirm the optimizer produces the intended pattern, and the proposed prostrate beam substantially extends coverage distance compared with conventional wide-beam benchmarks.
conclusion: Environment-aware beam shaping offers a practical route to improved broadcast coverage in centimeter-wave G-MIMO deployments.

title: Any Colour You Like, As Long As It's Uip: Semi-simplicial Types From Weakenings And Thinnings
authors: Thorsten Altenkirch
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explain an attempt to define semi-simplicial types (SST) in homotopy type theory by first defining a small type theory whose contexts are exactly the data of semi-simplicial types, constructing [MATH] uniformly in that syntax, and then interpreting the syntax in the universe. The syntax can be defined without any truncation and without K, and the construction of [MATH] goes through. The naive interpretation does not: it transports along the semantic images of equations that hold only propositionally, and making these transports agree needs uniqueness of identity proofs (UIP) for the semantic types. Moving the problem into the syntax, by making composition a constructor of a higher inductive-inductive type (HIIT), does not remove it either: it reappears as a coherence problem in the syntax. Fording the HIIT (storing equations instead of computed indices), with conditional rules, makes the syntax provably a set. This is UIP for the syntax, obtained by encode-decode, and it does not by itself restrict the semantics; but the naive interpretation of the conditional rules again needs UIP for the semantic types. A semantics into groupoids that avoids UIP will be discussed in a separate note. The Agda development accompanying this note is in the repository [URL].
tldr: A technical note in homotopy type theory attempting to define semi-simplicial types via a small internal type theory whose contexts are semi-simplicial data, showing that the naive interpretation requires uniqueness of identity proofs (UIP).
motivation: Defining semi-simplicial types in homotopy type theory is a long-standing open problem, and the author explores a syntactic route via weakenings and thinnings to avoid the coherence obstructions of direct definitions.
method: The author defines a bespoke type theory whose contexts are semi-simplicial data, constructs the required operation uniformly in that syntax (without truncation or K), then interprets the syntax in the universe; a higher inductive-inductive (HIIT) formulation is also Fording the composition operation with conditional rules to make the syntax a set.
result: The syntax itself can be defined and proved to be a set via encode-decode, but the naive semantic interpretation transports along propositional equations and requires UIP for the semantic types; moving composition into the syntax as a HIIT constructor only relocates the problem as a syntactic coherence issue.
conclusion: The syntactic approach to semi-simplicial types does not by itself resolve the interpretation problem; a groupoid-valued semantics avoiding UIP is deferred to a separate note.

title: Formalizing Cooperation And Competition: An AI-Assisted Mathematical Addendum To A 2018 Planning Thesis
authors: Haitham Masaud Amar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.29637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an AI-assisted mathematical addendum to Strategic Trip Planning: Striking a Balance Between Competition and Cooperation (Amar, 2018). We reconstruct selected relationships between strategic choice, cooperative stability, participant approval and enforcement. The thesis's Nash-to-core proposition is under-specified until outsider opportunities are stated. We verify two-person implications under fixed outsiders and explicit efficiency conditions. Under isolation, the original example has an empty TU core; its funded counterpart uses an explicit external subsidy. For a monotone resource model we characterize the exact financing gap.
